summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen shot and fatally wounded Tim Confoy, a Havlin's Theater stage hand, in Allen's saloon at 619 Market Street after Confoy appeared to reach for a revolver.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, February 26, 1899, page 11.

facts.fact: Just after 2 a.m. Allen shot Tim Confoy, a stage hand at Havlin's Theater, in his saloon at 619 Market Street; Confoy was hit by three bullets and taken to the City Dispensary and City Hospital in critical condition
Allen was arrested and held at the Chestnut Street station, later moved to the Four Courts holdover; about fifty people in the saloon were also taken in as witnesses
places: Chestnut Street police station, St. Louis

facts.fact: According to the bartender, when Confoy made a movement as if to draw a revolver, Allen drew a revolver in each hand and said he was too slow before firing
facts.quote: Oh, no, you're too bloody slow.

facts.fact: Allen said he did not draw until he saw Confoy try to draw his weapon
facts.quote: Then, you bet your life, I let the bloody fool have it, and have it right.

facts.fact: John Spencer, Confoy's companion, was wounded in the left hand by a stray bullet

notes: Story read only from the low-resolution page.jpg (zoomed); left edge of the first column is partly faint, so facts are medium confidence. Recrop the clipping to the story body below the ad and re-OCR. The paper also described Allen's resort as one of the toughest in the city, with a low class of customers.
